exposure: male factor infertility diagnosis (obstructive azoospermia, non-obstructive azoospermia, other male factor)
cohort: The study included 71,121 initial autologous IVF cycles from the SART CORS data (2016-2017) involving couples with male factor infertility, comparing those with obstructive azoospermia, non-obstructive azoospermia, and other non-azoospermic male factors.
finding: Couples with either non-obstructive or obstructive azoospermia show overall comparable ART and perinatal outcomes to couples with other male factor infertility, with success primarily influenced by both maternal and paternal age.
